A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MolParser work. The main text and complete six-page supplements are readable, and corresponding tables, figures, definitions and experiments can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: V2 reports original OCSR accuracy and throughput measurements, controlled ablations, molecular-property prediction results and qualitative cases (Tables 2–6 and supplementary figures).

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports annotation-correction statistics in Section 4.

M1.justification: The E-SMILES representation, Swin–MLP–BART architecture, curriculum training and active-learning procedure are retained. Decoder-prefix details clarify implementation. The reaction-parsing pipeline in new Section 6.5 already appears in v2 Section 13.

E1.justification: Training sources, OCSR benchmarks, ordinary-molecule and Markush WildMol evaluations, and five MoleculeNet tasks are unchanged. Reaction parsing was already demonstrated in v2's appendix, so its main-text subsection adds no task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the OCSR comparisons in Tables 2–3 and molecular-property comparisons in Table 6. Newly cited Markush-recognition works are discussed but not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: Benchmark sizes, metrics, model configurations, throughput measurement procedures and previously stated training settings match. V3 newly specifies 20 pretraining epochs; v2 gives no conflicting pretraining duration, so this is additional disclosure rather than an established protocol change.

E4.justification: Section 4 adds a limited analysis of how much human correction the annotation pipeline requires, distinguishing accepted pre-annotations from samples needing successive correction rounds. Existing training-data, model-scale and augmentation ablations, failure cases and the reaction example remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 6 ROC-AUC averages over five runs. Neither adds seeds, variability estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new annotation proportions describe correction effort rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: V3 adds annotation proportions: 56.04% directly accepted pre-annotations, 20.97% accepted after one correction, 13.87% after a second round and 9.13% requiring three or more rounds. Numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the existing graphical and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 9 retains the same E-SMILES syntax and index definitions. The revised wording about uncertain ring-attachment positions restates the existing any-position rule. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The core representation, dataset, recognition-performance, speed and downstream-utility claims are retained. Although v3's abstract replaces 'largest' with 'large-scale', the largest-dataset claim remains in the introduction and dataset sections, so it is not withdrawn from the paper.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges that molecular chirality is not fully exploited and proposes improving chirality handling and expanding real annotations. It also explains Markush representation and rendering bottlenecks. Previously documented overlap, charge and E-SMILES failure conditions remain.

D1.justification: Section 11 newly discloses 20 pretraining epochs and flattening visual features into decoder-prefix tokens. Section 8 adds a detector-model access link, updates the demo address and removes provisional anonymous-release wording. These improve documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: A new Markush Recognition paragraph adds four references: ChemSchematicResolver, Haupt's Markush reconstruction work, MarkushGrapher and Wang et al.'s multimodal chemical reconstruction work. It expands discussion of representation and data-generation difficulties while retaining the earlier bibliography and main research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 polishes several introductory, annotation, property-prediction and supplementary paragraphs, removes duplicated curriculum-learning prose and refines terminology. New Section 6.5 brings an existing appendix application into the main narrative; the overall organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 3 to page 4, Tables 2–3 are grouped on page 7, and Table 6 is enlarged. Table 5 headings and caption and Figure 4's caption are refined. Existing figure images and examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The added pretraining duration and decoder-input details, detector access information and annotation-effort breakdown modestly improve reproducibility and transparency. Additional Markush references and an explicit chirality limitation improve context and qualification. These are useful refinements to otherwise unchanged experimental evidence, rather than a substantial strengthening of validation.
